draft.title: Nuclear fusion
card: Fusion is when two light nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus. It releases energy. An example is hydrogen nuclei fusing to form helium.
Fusion powers the Sun and other stars. In the Sun, hydrogen is fused into helium in the core.
Nuclei are positively charged, so they repel each other. To fuse, they must be moving very fast and get very close. This needs extremely high temperatures and pressures, as in the core of the Sun.
Fusion is different from fission. Fusion joins light nuclei, while fission splits a heavy nucleus.
draft.remember: Fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier one and releases energy. It needs extreme temperature and pressure to overcome repulsion.

a.q: Why does fusion need extremely high temperatures?
opts: Nuclei must move fast enough to overcome their repulsion
Nuclei must be heavy enough to split into smaller ones
Neutrons must be slowed down so they are absorbed
Nuclei must be melted so they can be joined together
a.why: Nuclei are positively charged and repel each other. High temperature gives them enough speed to get close and fuse. Slowing neutrons is part of fission in a reactor, not fusion.
a.clue: What do two positive charges do when they approach?

b.q: Which process happens in the core of the Sun?
opts: Hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium
Uranium nuclei split into smaller nuclei
Helium nuclei split into hydrogen nuclei
Hydrogen burns with oxygen to form water
b.why: The Sun gets its energy from fusion of hydrogen into helium. Splitting uranium is fission, which is not what powers the Sun. Burning hydrogen is a chemical reaction and is not a nuclear process.
b.clue: Light nuclei join to form a heavier one.

a.best: Nuclei must move fast enough to overcome their repulsion

b.best: Hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium

proposal.title: Nuclear fusion

a.q: Why does fusion need extremely high temperatures?
opts: Nuclei must move fast enough to overcome their repulsion
Nuclei must be heavy enough to split into smaller ones
Heat makes the nuclei attract each other more strongly
Nuclei must be melted so they can be joined together
a.why: Nuclei are positively charged and repel each other. High temperature gives them enough speed to get close and fuse. Heat does not make nuclei attract: they still repel, and speed is what lets them get close anyway.
